question.prompt: Should the out-of-range quantity rejection path be restored by raising the scenario/test pair budget from 2 to 3?

options.label: Keep budget 2
options.detail: Leave the quantity rejection path out of this run and rely on gap-1 to carry the missing oracle forward.

options.label: Raise to 3
options.detail: Include a separate negative scenario and test for quantities 0 and 501 being blocked before add-to-quote.

content.risk_rationale: The evicted path covers an important quantity boundary failure, but it ranked below the retained pricing and compatibility rules because the PRD does not define the rejection mechanism and a prior gap already captures that missing oracle.

content.title: Configure a workstation with valid boundary quantities and immediate price updates
content.intent: Prove a workstation configuration remains orderable across representative valid option combinations, the running unit price updates immediately as selections change, and the configuration can be added with the valid boundary quantities 1 and 500.
content.technique_notes: Used equivalence partitioning for processor/memory profile, storage, and operating system choices; used boundary value analysis on quantity via expand_bva over 1..500, which produced [0,1,2,499,500,501] and retained the valid in-range boundaries 1 and 500 for this outcome-identical path; used covering_array with strength=3 because money risk applies and no override was present, grouping the constrained processor-memory choices as cpu_memory_profile to respect the 64 GB compatibility rule while covering 3-way interactions across cpu_memory_profile × storage × os × quantity in 12 valid combinations.

content.title: Enforce visible compatibility rules on a laptop configuration
content.intent: Prove a laptop configuration keeps incompatible choices visible and disabled with their reasons, and that downgrading the processor from a 64 GB selection auto-corrects memory to 32 GB with the exact warning message.
content.technique_notes: Used negative/error coverage for incompatible selections on the rendered web form, plus state/flow coverage for the downgrade-triggered auto-correction. Used equivalence partitioning to choose one representative laptop path with two incompatible rule manifestations: laptop-only storage restriction and 64 GB memory downgrade correction. No covering array was needed because the path centers on distinct incompatibility outcomes rather than outcome-identical cross-input variation.

parameters.autocorrect_message: 64 GB memory requires Core Ultra 9 — memory changed to 32 GB

judgements.rationale: [applicability] Applied the Web form profile because the configurator is a rendered B2B web application with selectable component fields, quantity entry, disabled choices, and an Add to Quote action.

[applicability] Applied equivalence partitioning because processor, memory, storage, operating system, and quantity each have discrete representative values with the same expected outcome inside valid or invalid classes.
[applicability] Applied boundary value analysis only to quantity because the PRD states an ordered numeric range of minimum 1 and maximum 500.

[applicability] Applied state/flow analysis to the processor downgrade rule because the observable outcome depends on a transition from a valid Core Ultra 9 + 64 GB state to a downgraded processor state.

[applicability] Did not apply auth, concurrency, notification, mobile-native, or search/list techniques because this use-case evidence contains no login gate, shared-writer race, out-of-band effect, native-app surface, or result-set semantics.
[value_score] Scored highest because it exercises the revenue-relevant price and orderability path while collapsing many valid combinations into one bounded scenario.
[value_score] Scored second because it concentrates the mandatory compatibility enforcement behaviors that prevent invalid configurations from being quoted silently.
[value_score] Scored below the top two because its rejection oracle is underspecified by the PRD, reducing near-term executability under the pair budget.
